title: Spinach and Feta Filling
subtitle: classic Greek filling for pastry, pies, or served as a side
excerpt: This filling is used in spanakopita and spinach pies across Greece and the broader Mediterranean. It works in filo pastry, puff pastry, or as a simple side dish. Dill and nutmeg are key to the flavour.
sourceNotes: The filling for spanakopita, the Greek spinach and cheese pie. Eaten across Greece, Turkey, and the broader Mediterranean. Dill and nutmeg are the characteristic seasonings.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked filling for up to 2 months. Defrost fully and squeeze out any excess liquid before using.
recipe.batchNotes: Easy to double. Good as a filling for multiple pies or pastry parcels.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead and keep chilled.

content.text: The most important step is removing as much water as possible from the spinach. Excess moisture will make pastry soggy and the filling loose. Squeeze the defrosted spinach hard in your hands or in a clean tea towel.
Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the squeezed spinach. Stir and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until any remaining moisture evaporates.
Remove from heat. Cool slightly. Transfer to a bowl.
Add the crumbled feta, beaten eggs, dill, and nutmeg. Season with black pepper only -- the feta will add enough salt.
Mix well. Taste and adjust seasoning. Use immediately or refrigerate.

items.fix: Squeeze again in a clean cloth and cook off any remaining moisture in the pan.
Rinse feta under cold water before crumbling.

content.text: Spinach and feta is one of the most important flavour combinations in Greek cooking. It forms the filling for spanakopita, the classic filo pie eaten for breakfast, lunch, and dinner across Greece. The same filling works in puff pastry, in small parcels, or simply baked on its own. Dill is the herb most closely associated with this dish in Greek tradition.
